body:
### Summary

I recently started using Renovate, and pull requests from the Renovate lock file maintenance (https://github.com/DigitalEarthSweden/digital-earth-sweden-community/pull/167) sorts the resolution markers in a different order than single-package updates (https://github.com/DigitalEarthSweden/digital-earth-sweden-community/pull/168). For the linked pull requests that are made only a few hours apart, the consequence is that the difference for the package update is just a re-shuffling of the resolution markers without changing the version in uv.lock.

I don't know how Renovate works internally, but both pull requests were made with the same Renovate Docker image pinned by the hash of v44.104.2. Looking around in uv, #21000 with uv 0.12.4 seems to have introduced the current sorting of resolution markers, and I believe the Renovate image is recent enough to use that version of uv. There is nothing in the Renovate configuration we use that restricts the uv version used, and `tool.uv` in `pyproject.toml` only contains `exclude-newer = "7 days"`.

I asked a colleague who fed the information into an LLM and got the suggestion that there was a difference between `uv lock --upgrade-package rioxarray` feeding resolution markers into the resolver and grouping by Python version whereas `uv lock --upgrade` nests by platform followed by Python version.

The summary of the LLM output is mine so there's a risk that I misunderstood something while making the summary, and on top of that there's the usual risk that the LLM is hallucinating so I'm summarizing junk information.

### Platform

Renovate docker image in Github action running Ubuntu 26.04

### Version

I'm guessing 0.12.19, and feel fairly sure it's at least >=0.12.4

### Python version

3.14
title: Varying order of resolution-markers from the same `pyproject.toml`
